Hand sawing, cutting and diamond drilling should be used to prepare and trim
the sample. Adequate protection from the elements should be provided. Final
exposure and trimming of the sample to fit the loading frame and the testing
itself should all be completed with minimum delay to avold possible significant
changes In the mofsture and stress conditions of the sample. If tests are
carried out below the water table, precautions should be taken to avoltd the
effects of water pressure and seepage (see Section 29.1.2),

Where it Is intended to test one discontinuity only, care has to be taken
to avoid disturbance to the surface of the discontinuity, and to prepare the
sample so that the forces are applied correctly in the plane of the
discontinuity. The spatial orlentation of the discontinuity should be defined by
dip direction and dip measurements.

Where drained conditions are required, sultable drainage layers can be
inserted around the sample and on the loaded upper surface.

With the borehole shear device, there is no sample preparation as such,
but care is required during the formation of the borehole so as to limit
disturbance of the surrounding soil (Bauer & Demartinecourt, 1985).

IO.3 TEST ARRANGEMENT

The equipment for applying the normal load can consist of welghts,
kentledge, hydraulfe rams, flat Jacks acting against the excavation roof, or an
anchor system. The reaction system should ensure the uniform transfer of the
normal loads to the test sample and minimum resistance to the shear
displacement, e.g. by the use of low-friction devices such as ball seatings or
rofers ( Brown, 1981). A porous piston or other sultable medium can be used
to distribute the load where drained conditions are required. The alignment of
the force needs to be maintatned during the test.

The shearing force application system should ensure that the load Is
applied untformly over the plane of shearing, and that the lo2zd and geometrical
centroids are matched to eliminate movement. Where an Inclined shear force
ts required, the resultant of the shear force should pass through the centre of
the base of the shearing plane (Brown, 1981). Jf a constant normal load Is
required for this type of test, suitable reduction has to be made to the applied
normal load during testing to compensate for the Increase In vertical
component with Increasing shear force. The shear force application can be
developed by similar means to the normal loading. in both cases, care has to
be taken to ensure that the ground reaction does not extend to the sample.
The reaction system can frequently be provided by the excavation sidewalls.
fn certain cases, It may be necessary to provide the shear force by traction on
a system anchored by piles or cables. Sufficient travel [n the shear force
application system should be provided so that the complete test can be run
without interruption.
